sentences.i: and then traveled on until we came to Damascus.
sentences.n: ilā an with a following verb means 'until'.

sentences.t: فَرَأَيْنَاهَا مَدِينَةً ذَاتَ أَشْجَارٍ وَأَنْهَارٍ وَأَثْمَارٍ وَأَطْيَارٍ كَأَنَّهَا جَنَّةٌ فِيهَا مِنْ كُلِّ فَاكِهَةٍ
sentences.tr: fa-raʾaynāhā madīnatan dhāta ashjārin wa-anhārin wa-athmārin wa-aṭyārin ka-annahā jannatun fīhā min kulli fākihatin
sentences.l: So we saw it a city possessor-of trees and rivers and fruits and birds, as-if-it a garden; in it [is] of every fruit.
sentences.i: We found it a city of trees and rivers, of fruits and birds, as though it were a garden, with every kind of fruit within it.
sentences.n: A rhymed run: ashjār, anhār, athmār, aṭyār all end in -ār. The sentence carries over onto the next printed page, so 'of every fruit' lands just before the next unit.

sentences.t: فَنَزَلْنَا فِي بَعْضِ الْخَانَاتِ وَوَقَفُوا أَعْمَامِي بِا عُوا وَاشْتَرَوْا
sentences.tr: fa-nazalnā fī baʿḍi al-khānāti wa-waqafū aʿmāmī bā ʿū wa-ishtarawā
sentences.l: So we alighted in some of the inns, and they stood, my uncles, they sold and bought.
sentences.i: We put up at one of the inns, and my uncles set about their trading, selling and buying.
sentences.n: The print has the verb 'they stood' (waqafū) after the plural pronoun and before the subject 'my uncles', a Middle Arabic agreement: the verb carries its own plural ending even when the noun follows. 'Stood' here has the sense 'applied themselves to'. The print splits bāʿū (they sold) into two pieces.

sentences.t: وَبَاعُوا أَيْضًا بِضَاعَتِي فَرَبِحَ الدِّرْهَمُ خَمْسَةَ دَرَاهِمَ فَفَرِحْتُ بِالرِّبْحِ
sentences.tr: wa-bāʿū ayḍan biḍāʿatī fa-rabiḥa al-dirhamu khamsata darāhima fa-fariḥtu bi-al-ribḥi
sentences.l: And they sold also my-merchandise, and the dirham profited five dirhams, and I rejoiced in-the-profit.
sentences.i: They sold my merchandise too, and every dirham made a profit of five dirhams, and I rejoiced in the gain.
sentences.n: 'The dirham profited five dirhams' means each coin invested earned five more, a profit of 500 percent. The ordinary Arabic for 'profit' is the verb with a direct object, as here. bi- after fariḥa marks the thing rejoiced in.

sentences.t: وَخَلَّوْنِي أَعْمَامِي وَتَوَجَّهُوا إِلَى مِصْرَ فَقَعَدْتُ بَعْدَهُمْ
sentences.tr: wa-khallawnī aʿmāmī wa-tawajjahū ilā Miṣra fa-qaʿadtu baʿdahum
sentences.l: And they left-me, my uncles, and went-toward Miṣr, and I sat after them.
sentences.i: My uncles left me there and went on to Egypt, and I stayed behind them,
sentences.n: Again the verb comes before the plural subject with its plural ending: khallawnī aʿmāmī, 'they left me, my uncles'. The father's wish, that the boy not go on to Egypt, is being carried out.

sentences.t: وَمَكَثْتُ فِي قَاعَةٍ مَلِيحَةِ الْبُنْيَانِ يَعْجِزُ عَنْ وَصْفِهَا اللِّسَانُ آجَرْتُهَا كُلَّ شَهْرٍ دِينَارَيْنِ
sentences.tr: wa-makathtu fī qāʿatin malīḥati al-bunyāni yaʿjizu ʿan waṣfihā al-lisānu ājartuhā kulla shahrin dīnārayni
sentences.l: And I stayed in a hall, fine of the-construction, the-tongue is-unable to describe it; I-rented it each month [for] two dinars.
sentences.i: and I took up my lodging in a hall of fine construction, beyond the power of the tongue to describe; I rented it at two dinars a month.
sentences.n: Another rhyme: al-bunyān and al-lisān. The word ājartuhā is printed with a madda on the first letter. I read it as the verb 'I rented it' (ājara, strictly 'to let' but used loosely); if the print meant a noun, ujratuhā, 'its rent', the sense is nearly the same. qāʿa is a ground-floor hall or lodging.

sentences.t: فَأَقَمْتُ آكُلُ وَأَشْرَبُ حَتَّى صَرَفْتُ الْمَالَ الَّذِي مَعِي
sentences.tr: fa-aqamtu ākulu wa-ashrabu ḥattā ṣaraftu al-māla alladhī maʿī
sentences.l: So I stayed eating and drinking until I spent the money which [was] with me.
sentences.i: I stayed on, eating and drinking, until I had spent all the money I had with me.
sentences.n: 'I stayed, I eat and drink' is a common way of saying 'I went on eating and drinking', with the second verb in the present indicative.

sentences.t: فَفِي يَوْمٍ مِنْ بَعْضِ الْأَيَّامِ أَنَا قَاعِدٌ عَلَى بَابِ الْقَاعَةِ وَإِذَا بِصَبِيَّةٍ أَقْبَلَتْ وَهِيَ لَابِسَةٌ أَفْخَرَ الْمَلَابِسِ
sentences.tr: fa-fī yawmin min baʿḍi al-ayyāmi anā qāʿidun ʿalā bābi al-qāʿati wa-idhā bi-ṣabiyyatin aqbalat wa-hiya lābisatun afkhara al-malābisi
sentences.l: So on a day of some of the days, I [was] sitting on the door of the hall, and behold, a girl came-on, and she wearing the most-splendid of garments.
sentences.i: One day, as I sat at the door of the hall, behold, a young woman came up, wearing the most splendid of clothes;
sentences.n: 'On a day of some of the days' is the ordinary storyteller's 'one day'. wa-idhā bi- marks a sudden arrival, 'and behold'; the bi- only introduces what appears. ṣabiyya is a young woman or girl.

sentences.t: مَا رَأَتْ عَيْنِي أَفْخَرَ مِنْهَا
sentences.tr: mā raʾat ʿaynī afkhara minhā
sentences.l: Not saw my-eye [anything] more-splendid than-her.
sentences.i: my eye had never seen finer.
sentences.n: The print gives the word for 'saw' here (raʾat) with the hamza already written, which I keep as printed.

sentences.t: فَغَمَزْتُ عَلَيْهَا فَمَا قَصَّرَتْ حَتَّى صَارَتْ دَاخِلَ الْبَابِ
sentences.tr: fa-ghamaztu ʿalayhā fa-mā qaṣṣarat ḥattā ṣārat dākhila al-bābi
sentences.l: So I winked at-her, and she did-not fall-short until she became inside the door.
sentences.i: I gave her a wink, and she did not hold back, but came inside the door.
sentences.n: ghamaza ʿalā means to make a sign to someone with the eye. qaṣṣara here means 'hesitate, fall short'.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا دَخَلْتُ أَنَا مَعَهَا فَرَدَدْتُ الْبَابَ عَلَيَّ وَعَلَيْهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā dakhaltu anā maʿahā fa-radadtu al-bāba ʿalayya wa-ʿalayhā
sentences.l: So when I entered, I, with her, I shut the door upon me and upon her
sentences.i: When I had gone in with her, I shut the door on myself and on her,
sentences.n: 'Shut the door upon me and upon her' means: shut us in together.

sentences.t: وَكَشَفَتْ نِقَابَهَا عَنْ وَجْهِهَا وَقَلَعَتْ إِزَارَهَا فَوَجَدْتُهَا بَدِيعَةً فِي الْجَمَالِ
sentences.tr: wa-kashafat niqābahā ʿan wajhihā wa-qalaʿat izārahā fa-wajadtuhā badīʿatan fī al-jamāli
sentences.l: And she uncovered her-veil from her-face, and she took-off her-wrap, and I found-her wondrous in beauty.
sentences.i: She lifted the veil from her face and took off her outer wrap, and I found her of wondrous beauty.
sentences.n: The subject changes without warning: the 'she' who unveils is the young woman, and the 'I' of fa-wajadtuhā is the narrator. izār is the large wrap worn over the clothes out of doors. qalaʿa is 'to pull off', common in the Nights.

sentences.t: فَتَمَكَّنَ حُبُّهَا مِنْ قَلْبِي
sentences.tr: fa-tamakkana ḥubbuhā min qalbī
sentences.l: So her-love took-firm-hold of my-heart.
sentences.i: And love of her took firm hold of my heart.

sentences.t: فَقُمْتُ وَجِبْتُ خُوبَخَهْ مِنْ أَطْيَبِ الْمَأْكُولِ وَالْفَاكِهَةِ وَمَا يَحْتَاجُ إِلَيْهِ الْمَقَامُ وَأَتَيْتُ بِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qumtu wa-jibtu khūbakhah min aṭyabi al-maʾkūli wa-al-fākihati wa-mā yaḥtāju ilayhi al-maqāmu wa-ataytu bihi
sentences.l: So I arose, and I fetched a khūbakha [obscure] of the choicest of the edibles and the fruit, and what the occasion needs of it, and I came with it.
sentences.i: I rose and fetched a feast of the choicest foods and fruit, and all that the occasion required, and brought it in.
sentences.n: The word printed khūbakha (خوبخه) is obscure and may be corrupt; the sense of a spread or a basketful, as the next words ('of the choicest foods') suggest, is a guess. jibtu is colloquial for 'I fetched' (from jāba); ataytu bihi is the usual 'I brought it', with the verb choosing bi-.

sentences.t: وَأَكَلْنَا وَلَعِبْنَا وَبَعْدَ اللَّعِبِ شَرِبْنَا حَتَّى سَكِرْنَا
sentences.tr: wa-akalnā wa-laʿibnā wa-baʿda al-laʿibi sharibnā ḥattā sakirnā
sentences.l: And we ate, and we played, and after the play we drank until we were-drunk.
sentences.i: We ate, we toyed with one another, and after the toying we drank, until we were drunk.
sentences.n: laʿiba, 'to play', is here amorous play. Notice the ordering: love-play, then wine.

sentences.t: فَقُمْتُ وَنِمْتُ مَعَهَا فِي أَطْيَبِ لَيْلَةٍ إِلَى الصَّبَاحِ
sentences.tr: fa-qumtu wa-nimtu maʿahā fī aṭyabi laylatin ilā al-ṣabāḥi
sentences.l: So I arose and I lay with her in the sweetest night until the morning.
sentences.i: Then I rose and lay with her, in the sweetest of nights, until morning.
sentences.n: nāma maʿahā, 'to sleep with her', is plain: they sleep together.

sentences.t: وَأَعْطَيْتُ لَهَا عَشَرَةَ دَنَانِيرَ فَعَبَسَتْ وَجْهَهَا وَقَطَّبَتْ حَاجِبَيْهَا وَزَعِلَتْ وَقَالَتْ
sentences.tr: wa-aʿṭaytu lahā ʿasharata danānīra fa-ʿabasat wajhahā wa-qaṭṭabat ḥājibayhā wa-zaʿilat wa-qālat
sentences.l: And I gave to-her ten dinars, and she frowned [with] her-face and knitted her-brows and was-vexed, and she said:
sentences.i: I gave her ten dinars; she scowled, knit her brows, grew vexed, and said:
sentences.n: Her angry speech begins here and runs on into the next unit. ʿabasat wajhahā puts 'face' in the accusative as a closer specification, 'she frowned (as to) her face'.

sentences.t: أُفٍّ لَكُمْ يَامُوَاصِلَةُ كَأَنَّكَ تَظُنُّ أَنِّي طَامِعَةٌ فِي مَالِكَ
sentences.tr: uffin lakum yāmuwāṣilatu ka-annaka taẓunnu annī ṭāmiʿatun fī mālika
sentences.l: Fie to-you, O company-keepers, as-if-you think that-I [am] covetous in your wealth
sentences.i: Fie upon you, you keepers of company! You seem to think that I am greedy for your wealth.
sentences.n: Her speech answers his gift of ten dinars, which she takes as payment. yāmuwāṣila is printed as one word; muwāṣila is obscure: I read it as 'those who keep up a connection (with a lover)', but the singular ka-annaka that follows suggests she means him alone, so the word may be corrupt. uff is the exclamation of disgust.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَخْرَجَتْ مِنْ جَيْبِ قَمِيصِهَا خَمْسَةَ عَشَرَ دِينَارًا وَخَلَّتْ قُدَّامِي
sentences.tr: thumma akhrajat min jaybi qamīṣihā khamsata ʿashara dīnāran wa-khallat quddāmī
sentences.l: Then she brought-out from the pocket of her shirt fifteen dinar, and left in-front-of-me
sentences.i: Then she drew fifteen dinars from the pocket of her shirt and laid them before me,
sentences.n: khallat, 'she left, set down', has the dinars understood as its object; quddāmī, 'in front of me', is the everyday word for 'before'.

sentences.t: وَقَالَتْ وَاللَّهِ إِنْ لَمْ تَأْخُذْهَا لَمْ أَعُدْ إِلَيْكَ
sentences.tr: wa-qālat wa-allāhi in lam taʾkhudhhā lam aʿud ilayka
sentences.l: and she said, 'By-God, if not you-take them, not I-return to-you'
sentences.i: and said, 'By God, if you do not take them, I shall never come back to you.'

sentences.t: فَقَبِلْتُهَا مِنْهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qabiltuhā minhā
sentences.l: So I accepted them from her

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَتْ يَا حَبِيبِي انْتَظِرْنِي بَعْدَ ثَلٰثَةِ أَيَّامٍ بَيْنَ الْمَغْرِبِ وَالْعِشَاءِ أَكُونُ عِنْدَكَ وَعَبِّ لَنَا بِهَٰذِهِ الدَّنَانِيرِ مِثْلَ هَٰذَا
sentences.tr: thumma qālat yā ḥabībī intaẓirnī baʿda thalāthati ayyāmin bayna al-maghribi wa-al-ʿishāʾi akūnu ʿindaka wa-ʿabbi lanā bi-hādhihi al-danānīri mithla hādhā
sentences.l: Then she said: 'O my beloved, wait-for-me after three of-days, between the sunset and the night-fall; I-will-be with-you; and stock for-us with these the-dinars like this.'
sentences.i: Then she said, 'My darling, wait for me three days from now, between sunset and nightfall, and I shall be with you; and lay in provisions for us with these dinars, as you did before.'
sentences.n: ʿabbi is the imperative of ʿabbā, 'to fill, pack, make ready', a colloquial verb; the narrator answers with it below (ʿabbaytu lahā al-maqām, 'I made the place ready for her'): food, wine and candles for the evening. akūnu ʿindaka, 'I shall be with you', follows the command with no 'and', as spoken Arabic does.

sentences.t: وَوَدَّعَتْنِي وَانْصَرَفَتْ فَغَابَ عَقْلِي مَعَهَا
sentences.tr: wa-waddaʿatnī wa-inṣarafat fa-ghāba ʿaqlī maʿahā
sentences.l: and she bade-me-farewell and went-away, and my mind went-absent with-her
sentences.i: She bade me farewell and left, and my wits departed with her.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا مَضَتِ الْأَيَّامُ الثَّلٰثَةُ أَتَتْ وَعَلَيْهَا مِنَ الْمُزَرْكَشِ وَالْحُلِيِّ وَالْحُلَلِ أَعْظَمُ مِمَّا كَانَ عَلَيْهَا أَوَّلًا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā maḍati al-ayyāmu al-thalāthatu atat wa-ʿalayhā mina al-muzarkashi wa-al-ḥuliyyi wa-al-ḥulali aʿẓamu mimmā kāna ʿalayhā awwalan
sentences.l: So when passed the days the-three, she-came, and on-her [was] of the gold-embroidered and the jewels and the robes [something] greater than what was on-her at-first
sentences.i: When the three days had passed she came, and the embroidered stuffs, jewels and robes she wore were grander than those she had worn the first time.
sentences.n: al-muzarkash is cloth worked with gold thread. aʿẓamu mimmā, 'greater than what', means 'more splendid than'.

sentences.t: وَكُنْتُ عَبَّيْتُ لَهَا الْمَقَامَ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَحْضُرَ
sentences.tr: wa-kuntu ʿabbaytu lahā al-maqāma qabla an taḥḍura
sentences.l: and I had stocked for-her the place before that she-came
sentences.i: I had made the place ready for her before she arrived.
sentences.n: al-maqām, literally 'the standing-place', is the room set out for the party: carpets, food, drink.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَكَلْنَا وَشَرِبْنَا وَنِمْنَا مِثْلَ الْعَادَةِ إِلَى الصَّبَاحِ
sentences.tr: thumma akalnā wa-sharibnā wa-nimnā mithla al-ʿādati ilā al-ṣabāḥi
sentences.l: Then we-ate and we-drank and we-slept like the custom until the morning
sentences.i: Then we ate and drank and slept, as was our custom, until morning.

sentences.t: أَعْطَتْنِي خَمْسَهَ عَشَرَ دَنَانِيرَ وَاعَدَتْنِي بَعْدَ ثَلٰثَةِ أَيَّامٍ تَحْضُرُ عِنْدِي
sentences.tr: aʿṭatnī khamsah ʿashara danānīra wāʿadatnī baʿda thalāthati ayyāmin taḥḍuru ʿindī
sentences.l: She gave-me fifteen dinars; she-made-an-appointment-with-me after three of-days, she-would-come at-me
sentences.i: She gave me fifteen dinars and promised that in three days she would come to me again.
sentences.n: The edition prints khamsah with a final hāʾ and puts the plural danānīr after the number, where Classical Arabic wants the singular; I vocalise what is printed. wāʿadatnī is read as one verb (form III, 'make an appointment with'), with no separate 'and'; the bare taḥḍuru after it, 'she would come', is spoken-style Arabic.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ عَبَّيْتُ لَهَا الْمَقَامَ وَبَعْدَ أَيَّامٍ حَضَرَتْ فِي قُمَاشٍ أَعْظَمَ مِنَ الْأَوَّلِ وَالثَّانِي
sentences.tr: thumma ʿabbaytu lahā al-maqāma wa-baʿda ayyāmin ḥaḍarat fī qumāshin aʿẓama mina al-awwali wa-al-thānī
sentences.l: Then I stocked for-her the place, and after days she-attended in cloth greater than the first and the second
sentences.i: Then I made the place ready for her again, and some days later she came in garments grander than on the first or the second visit.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَتْ يَا سَيِّدِي مَا أَنَا مَلِيحَةٌ فَقُلْتُ إِي وَاللَّهِ
sentences.tr: thumma qālat yā sayyidī mā anā malīḥatun fa-qultu ī wa-allāhi
sentences.l: Then she said: 'O my master, [mā] I [am] pretty?' and I said: 'Yes, by-God.'
sentences.i: Then she said, 'My lord, am I not lovely?' and I said, 'Yes, by God.'
sentences.n: mā plus a pronoun and a predicate works as a negative question, 'am I not ...?'; it comes back below (mā hiya aẓrafu minnī). ī wa-allāh is 'yes, by God', the particle of assent.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ هَلْ تَأْذَنُ لِي أَنْ أَجِيبَ مَعِي صَبِيَّةً أَحْسَنَ مِنِّي وَأَصْغَرَ سِنًّامِنِّي
sentences.tr: fa-qultu hal taʾdhanu lī an ajība maʿī ṣabiyyatan aḥsana minnī wa-aṣghara sinnamminnī
sentences.l: So I said: 'Do you permit me that I-bring with-me a girl, better than-me and smaller of-age than-me,
sentences.i: Then she said, 'Will you permit me to bring with me a girl, lovelier than I and younger,
sentences.n: The edition prints faqultu, 'so I said', but the speaker must be the lady (the girl has asked 'me', and 'with me' follows), so this looks like a slip for faqālat, 'so she said'; I point what is printed and translate the sense. ajība is the colloquial 'bring' (Classical aḥḍara or jāʾa bi-). sinnamminnī, 'in age than me', is printed as one word; the gloss splits it.

sentences.t: حَتَّى تَلْعَبَ مَعَنَا وَتَضْحَكَ وَإِيَّا هَا وَتَنْشَرِحَ قَلْبُهَا لِأَنَّهَا مَحْزُونَةٌ مِنْ زَمَانٍ
sentences.tr: ḥattā talʿaba maʿanā wa-taḍḥaka wa-iyyā hā wa-tanshariḥa qalbuhā li-annahā maḥzūnatun min zamānin
sentences.l: so-that she-plays with-us and laughs, and [iyyā hā], and her-heart opens-wide, because-she [is] sorrowful from a-time,
sentences.i: so that she may play and laugh with us, and her heart may be eased, for she has long been sorrowful,
sentences.n: The printed wa-iyyā hā is two words: iyyā is the base of the object pronoun, here left without a verb. The text is elliptical or corrupt there; the sense seems to be 'and [we shall cheer] her'. The verb tanshariḥa is feminine with qalbuhā, 'her heart', agreeing with the girl rather than with the noun. min zamān, 'for a long time', is spoken-style.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ سَأَلَتْنِي أَنْ تَخْرُجَ مَعِي وَتَبَاتَ مَعِي
sentences.tr: wa-qad saʾalatnī an takhruja maʿī wa-tabāta maʿī
sentences.l: and indeed she-asked-me that she-go-out with-me and spend-the-night with-me
sentences.i: and she has asked me to let her go out with me and spend the night with me.'
sentences.n: The print has tbāt, with a long-ā shape of the verb bāta, 'to spend the night'; Classical Arabic would have tabīta. I point it as printed.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعْتُ كَلَامَهَا قُلْتُ إِي وَاللَّهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿtu kalāmahā qultu ī wa-allāhi
sentences.l: So when I-heard her speech I-said: 'Yes, by-God.'
sentences.i: When I heard her words I said, 'Yes, by God.'

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّنَا سَكِرْنَا وَنِمْنَا إِلَى الصَّبَاحِ فَأَخْرَجَتْ لِي خَمْسَةَ عَشْرَةَ دَنَانِيرَ
sentences.tr: thumma innanā sakirnā wa-nimnā ilā al-ṣabāḥi fa-akhrajat lī khamsata ʿashrata danānīra
sentences.l: Then indeed-we we-got-drunk and we-slept until the morning, and she-brought-out for-me fifteen dinars
sentences.i: Then we drank ourselves drunk and slept until morning, and she brought out fifteen dinars for me,
sentences.n: The edition spells the teen with tāʾ marbūṭa, ʿashrata, and again puts the plural danānīr after the number; I keep both as printed.

sentences.t: وَقَالَتْ زِدْ لَنَا الْمَقَامَ لِأَجْلِ الصَّبِيَّةِ الَّتِي تَأْتِي مَعِي
sentences.tr: wa-qālat zid lanā al-maqāma li-ajli al-ṣabiyyati allatī taʾtī maʿī
sentences.l: and she said: 'Increase for-us the place for the sake of the girl who comes with-me'
sentences.i: and said, 'Provide more for us on account of the girl who is coming with me.'

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهَا انْصَرَفَتْ فَلَمَّا كَانَ الْيَوْمُ الرَّابِعُ جَهَّزْتُ لَهَا الْمَقَامَ عَلَى الْعَادَةِ
sentences.tr: thumma innahā inṣarafat fa-lammā kāna al-yawmu al-rābiʿu jahhaztu lahā al-maqāma ʿalā al-ʿādati
sentences.l: Then indeed-she went-away; so when it-was the day the fourth, I-equipped for-her the place upon the custom
sentences.i: Then she went away; and when the fourth day came I prepared the place for her as usual.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَ بَعْدَ الْمَغْرِبِ وَإِذَا بِهَا أَتَتْ وَمَعَهَا وَاحِدَةٌ مَلْفُوفَةٌ بِإِزَارٍ فَدَخَلُوا وَجَلَسُوا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kāna baʿda al-maghribi wa-idhā bihā atat wa-maʿahā wāḥidatun malfūfatun bi-izārin fa-dakhalū wa-jalasū
sentences.l: So when it-was after the sunset, and-behold with-her she-came, and with-her one wrapped in-a-wrap; so they-entered and they-sat
sentences.i: Just after sunset, behold, she arrived, and with her another woman wrapped in a veil; and they came in and sat down.
sentences.n: wa-idhā bihā, 'and behold, her', is the usual way of announcing a sudden arrival; the bi- only marks what appears. The verbs dakhalū and jalasū are plural although only two women are meant, a spoken-style looseness. al-izār is the large wrap a woman drew round herself outdoors.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَيْتُهَا أَنْشَدْتُ شِعْرً
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾaytuhā anshadtu shiʿran
sentences.l: So when I-saw her I-recited poetry
sentences.i: When I saw her I recited verses:
sentences.n: The printed pronoun 'her' could point to either woman; the verses that follow praise the evening as a whole.

sentences.t:
مَا اَطْيَبَ وَقْتَنَا وَاهْنَى * وَالْعَاذِلُ غَائِبُ وَغَافِل
عِشْقٌ وَمَسَرَّةٌ وَسُكْرُ * اَلْعَقْلُ بِبَعْضِ ذَاكَ زَائِلْ
وَالْبَدْرُ يَلُوحُ فِي قِنَاعٍ * وَالْغُصْنُ يَمِيلُ فِي غَلَائِل
وَالْوَرْدُ عَلَى الْخُدُودِ غَضٌّ * وَالنَّرْجِسُ فِى الْعُيُونِ ذَابِل
وَالْعَيْشُ كَمَا اُحِبُّ صَافِ * وَالْاُنْسُ بِمَنْ اُحِبُّ كَامِل
sentences.tr:
mā aṭyaba waqtanā wa-ahnā * wa-al-ʿādhilu ghāʾibu wa-ghāfil
ʿishqun wa-masarratun wa-sukru * al-ʿaqlu bi-baʿḍi dhāka zāʾil
wa-al-badru yalūḥu fī qināʿin * wa-al-ghuṣnu yamīlu fī ghalāʾil
wa-al-wardu ʿalā al-khudūdi ghaḍḍun * wa-al-narjisu fī al-ʿuyūni dhābil
wa-al-ʿayshu ka-mā uḥibbu ṣāfi * wa-al-unsu bi-man uḥibbu kāmil
sentences.l:
How sweet our time and how pleasant * while the blamer [is] absent and heedless
Love and gladness and drunkenness * the mind through some of that [is] gone
And the full-moon shines in a-head-veil * and the branch sways in under-robes
And the rose on the cheeks [is] fresh * and the narcissus in the eyes [is] withered
And life as I love [it is] pure * and intimacy with whom I love [is] complete
sentences.i:
How sweet our hour, how pleasant,
with the censor absent and heedless;
Love and gladness and drunkenness,
and reason half undone by them.
The full moon shines from its veil,
the branch sways in its silks;
The rose is fresh upon the cheeks,
the narcissus languid in the eyes.
Life is just as I would have it, clear,
and the company of those I love is perfect.
sentences.n: The print points this poem, and I copy it as printed, including the fatḥa it puts on bare alif (اَطْيَبَ, اَلْعَقْلُ) and the dammas on اُحِبُّ and الْاُنْسُ, which are not hamzas. Several line-end vowels (غَافِل, زَائِل, غَلَائِل, ذَابِل, كَامِل) are kasras for the rhyme, and سُكْرُ, غَائِبُ and صَافِ lack their tanwīn; all are as printed. al-ʿādhil is the 'blamer' who scolds lovers, a stock figure of this verse. The narcissus 'withered' in the eyes is the drooping, languid eye of the beloved.

sentences.t: فَفَرِحْتُ وَأَوْقَدْتُ الشَّمْعَ وَالْتَقَيْتُهُمْ بِالْفَرَحِ وَالسُّرُورِ
sentences.tr: fa-fariḥtu wa-awqadtu al-shamʿa wa-iltaqaytuhum bi-al-faraḥi wa-al-surūri
sentences.l: So I-rejoiced and I-lit the candle and I-met-them with the joy and the gladness
sentences.i: I was glad, and I lit the candles and met them with joy and delight.
sentences.n: iltaqaytuhum, 'I met them', is the eighth form of laqiya; the plain laqaytuhum would mean the same.

sentences.t: فَقَامُوا وَخَفَّفُوا مَا عَلَيْهِمْ مِنَ الْقُمَاشِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāmū wa-khaffafū mā ʿalayhim mina al-qumāshi
sentences.l: so they-stood and they-lightened what [was] on-them of the cloth
sentences.i: They rose and lightened their dress, taking off their outer garments.
sentences.n: khaffafū, 'they lightened', means they shed the heavy outer layers of their street clothes.

sentences.t: وَكَشَفَتِ الصَّبِيَّةُ الْجَدِيدَةُ عَنْ وَجْهِهَا فَرَأَيْتُهَا كَالْبَدْرِ فِي تَمَامِهِ فَلَمْ أَرَأَحْسَنَ مِنْهَا
sentences.tr: wa-kashafati al-ṣabiyyatu al-jadīdatu ʿan wajhihā fa-raʾaytuhā ka-al-badri fī tamāmihi fa-lam ara aḥsana minhā
sentences.l: and the girl the-new uncovered from her-face, and I-saw her like the full-moon in its fullness, and I-did-not see better than-her
sentences.i: The new girl uncovered her face, and I saw her like the full moon at its fullest; I had never seen anyone lovelier.
sentences.n: fa-lam ara aḥsana minhā is printed as two words run together (araaḥsana); I point it as ara + aḥsana. ka- before al-badr is 'like': the moon at the full (tamām) is the stock image of a beauty.

sentences.t: فَقُمْتُ وَقَدَّمْتُ لَهُمُ الْأَ كْلَ وَالشُّرْبَ
sentences.tr: fa-qumtu wa-qaddamtu lahumu al-a kla wa-al-shurba
sentences.l: So I-stood and I-presented to-them the eating and the drinking
sentences.i: I got up and set food and drink before them.
sentences.n: The edition prints al-akl, 'the eating', as two words (الا كل); I point each part as printed.

sentences.t: فَأَكَلْنَا وَشَرِبْنَا وَصِرْتُ أُلْقِمُ الصَّبِيَّةَ الْجَدِيدَةَ وَأَمْلَاءُ لَهَا الْقَدَحَ وَأَشْرَبُ مَعَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-akalnā wa-sharibnā wa-ṣirtu ulqimu al-ṣabiyyata al-jadīdata wa-amlāʾu lahā al-qadaḥa wa-ashrabu maʿahā
sentences.l: So we-ate and we-drank, and I-became I-feed-morsels to-the girl the-new, and I-fill for-her the cup, and I-drink with-her
sentences.i: We ate and drank, and I took to feeding morsels to the new girl, filling her cup and drinking with her.
sentences.n: ulqimu is 'I put a morsel in her mouth', a gesture of lovers' courtesy. The print spells amlaʾu, 'I fill', with a hamza written after the alif (املاء), as in the noun for 'water'; the word is still the verb.

sentences.t: فَغَارَتِ الصَّبِيَّةُ الْأُولَى فِى الْبَاطِنِ ثُمَّ قَالَتْ بِاللَّهِ هَٰذِهِ الصَّبِيَّةُ مَا هِيَ أَظْرَفُ مِنِّي
sentences.tr: fa-ghārati al-ṣabiyyatu al-ūlā fī al-bāṭini thumma qālat bi-allāhi hādhihi al-ṣabiyyatu mā hiya aẓrafu minnī
sentences.l: So grew-jealous the girl the-first in the inside; then she said: 'By-God, this girl, [mā] she [is] more charming than-me?'
sentences.i: The first girl grew jealous in secret, and then said, 'By God, is this girl not lovelier than I?'
sentences.n: fī al-bāṭin, 'inwardly', means she hid her jealousy. bi-allāh here is the oath, 'by God'. mā hiya is again the negative question, 'is she not ...?'.

sentences.t: قُلْتُ إِي وَاللَّهِ قَالَتْ خَاطِرِي أَنْ تَنَامَ مَعَهَا قُلْتُ عَلَى رَأْسِي وَعَيْنِي
sentences.tr: qultu ī wa-allāhi qālat khāṭirī an tanāma maʿahā qultu ʿalā raʾsī wa-ʿaynī
sentences.l: I-said: 'Yes, by-God.' She-said: 'My-wish [is] that you-sleep with-her.' I-said: 'Upon my-head and my-eye.'
sentences.i: I said, 'Yes, by God.' She said, 'I should like you to sleep with her.' I said, 'Gladly, upon my head and my eye.'
sentences.n: khāṭirī, 'my wish, my inclination', is the spoken way of saying 'I would like'. ʿalā raʾsī wa-ʿaynī, 'upon my head and my eye', is a courteous formula of ready consent.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَامَتْ وَفَرَشَتْ لَنَا فَقُمْتُ رُحْتُ لِلصَّبِيَّةِ وَنِمْتُ إِلَى وَقْتِ الصُّبْحِ
sentences.tr: thumma qāmat wa-farashat lanā fa-qumtu ruḥtu li-al-ṣabiyyati wa-nimtu ilā waqti al-ṣubḥi
sentences.l: Then she stood and she-spread for-us; so I-stood, I-went to-the girl and I-slept until the time of-the dawn
sentences.i: Then she rose and spread the bedding for us; and I got up, went to the girl, and slept with her until the hour of dawn.
sentences.n: ruḥtu is printed without a conjunction after faqumtu: 'I rose, I went', a spoken-style pair of verbs. li-al-ṣabiyya: li- here is 'to', marking the goal of ruḥtu, 'I went to the girl'.

sentences.t: فَتَحَرَّكْتُ فَوَجَدْتُ رُوحِي فِي عَرَقٍ عَظِيمٍ فَحَسِبْتُ أَنِّي عَرْقَانُ
sentences.tr: fa-taḥarraktu fa-wajadtu rūḥī fī ʿaraqin ʿaẓīmin fa-ḥasibtu annī ʿarqānu
sentences.l: So I-moved, and I-found my-self in a-sweat great, and I-reckoned that-I [was] sweating
sentences.i: I stirred and found myself drenched in a great sweat, and I supposed that I was sweating.
sentences.n: rūḥī, literally 'my spirit', is the spoken way of saying 'myself'. ʿarqān is the adjective 'sweating'.

sentences.t: فَقَعَدْتُ أُنَبِّهُ الصَّبِيَّةَ وَهَزَيْتُ أَكْتَافَهَا فَتَدَ حْرَجَتْ رَأْسُهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qaʿadtu unabbihu al-ṣabiyyata wa-hazaytu aktāfahā fa-tada ḥrajat raʾsuhā
sentences.l: So I-sat I-awaken the girl and I-shook her shoulders, and rolled [tada ḥrajat] her head
sentences.i: I sat up to rouse the girl and shook her by the shoulders, and her head rolled ...
sentences.n: The sentence runs on into the next unit. The edition prints tadaḥrajat, 'rolled along', as two words (fatad ḥrajat); read it as one verb. hazaytu is the spoken form of hazaztu, 'I shook'.

sentences.t: مِنْ عَلَا الْوِسَادَةِ فَطَارَ عَقْلِي وَصَرَخْتُ وَقُلْتُ يَا جَمِيلَ السِّتْرِ سِتْرَكَ
sentences.tr: min ʿalā al-wisādati fa-ṭāra ʿaqlī wa-ṣarakhtu wa-qultu yā jamīla al-sitri sitraka
sentences.l: from upon the pillow, so flew my mind; and I shrieked and said: O fair-of-the-covering, your covering!
sentences.i: …from the pillow, and my wits flew from me. I cried out and said, "O You whose covering is fair, grant Your covering!"
sentences.n: The sentence continues from the previous unit: min ʿalā al-wisāda completes 'her head rolled …'. ʿalā is printed علا, with alif for ى; it is the ordinary preposition. The cry is addressed to God: jamīl al-sitr is a vocative construct, and sitraka is an accusative of petition ('[grant] your covering').

sentences.t: فَوَجَدْتُهَا مَذْبُوحَةً فَنَهَضْتُ عَلَى حَيْلِي وَقَدِ اسْوَدَّتِ الدُّنْيَا فِي عَيْنِي
sentences.tr: fa-wajadtuhā madhbūḥatan fa-nahaḍtu ʿalā ḥaylī wa-qadi iswaddati al-dunyā fī ʿaynī
sentences.l: then I found her slaughtered, then I rose upon my strength, and the world had blackened in my eye
sentences.i: I found her with her throat cut, and I got to my feet on what strength I had, while the world had turned black before my eyes.
sentences.n: ʿalā ḥaylī, 'on my strength', is how I read the printed حيلي (ḥayl, force, strength; Lane). The sense is that he got up by sheer effort.

sentences.t: وَطَلَبْتُ صَاحِبَتِي الْقَدِيمَةَ فَلَمْ أَجِدْهَا فَعَلِمْتُ أَنَّهَا هِى الَّتِي ذَبَحَتِ الصَّبِيَّةَ مِنْ غَيْرَتِهَا مِنْهَا
sentences.tr: wa-ṭalabtu ṣāḥibatī al-qadīmata fa-lam ajidhā fa-ʿalimtu annahā hiya allatī dhabaḥati al-ṣabiyyata min ghayratihā minhā
sentences.l: and I sought my companion the old-one, and I did not find her, so I knew that she, she was the-one-who slaughtered the girl out-of her jealousy of her
sentences.i: I looked for my former mistress and could not find her, and I knew that it was she who had cut the girl's throat, out of jealousy.
sentences.n: ṣāḥibatī al-qadīma, 'my old companion', is the woman he had before the girl. The separate pronoun hiya in 'annahā hiya allatī' stresses 'it was she, she, who'.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَاحَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّابِاللهِ الْعَلِيِّ الْعَظِيمِ كَيْفَ يَكُونُ عَمَلِي
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lāḥawla wa-lā quwwata illābi-allāhi al-ʿaliyyi al-ʿaẓīmi kayfa yakūnu ʿamalī
sentences.l: so I said: no-power and no-strength save with-God the high, the great; how will-be my doing?
sentences.i: And I said, "There is no might and no power save in God, the High, the Great." What was I to do?
sentences.n: The pious formula (the ḥawqala) is printed with lāḥawla and illābi-llāh each as one word, and I keep the words as printed.

sentences.t: فَتَفَكَّرْتُ سَاعَةً وَقُمْتُ قَلَعْتُ ثِيَابِي وَحَفَرْتُ فِى وَسَطِ الْقَاعَةِ حَفْرَةً
sentences.tr: fa-tafakkartu sāʿatan wa-qumtu qalaʿtu thiyābī wa-ḥafartu fī wasaṭi al-qāʿati ḥafratan
sentences.l: so I pondered an hour, and I rose, I took-off my clothes, and I dug in the middle of the hall a pit
sentences.i: I thought for an hour; then I got up, took off my clothes, and dug a pit in the middle of the hall.
sentences.n: wa-qumtu qalaʿtu: two perfects side by side with no 'and' between them, 'I got up, I took off', a common way for Middle Arabic to string actions. al-qāʿa is the ground-floor hall or reception room. The print reads حفرة and it is pointed ḥafra here ('a digging'); at its next mention it is pointed ḥufra, 'pit'.

sentences.t: وَأَخَذْتُ الصَّبِيَّةَ مَعَ مُصَاغِهَا وَجَعَلْتُهَا فِي الْحُفْرَةِ وَرَدَّيْتُ عَلَيْهَا التُّرَابَ وَالرُّخَامَ
sentences.tr: wa-akhadhtu al-ṣabiyyata maʿa muṣāghihā wa-jaʿaltuhā fī al-ḥufrati wa-raddaytu ʿalayhā al-turāba wa-al-rukhāma
sentences.l: and I took the girl with her wrought-jewellery and set her in the pit, and I threw-back upon her the earth and the marble
sentences.i: I took the girl, jewels and all, and laid her in the pit, and put back over her the earth and the marble flags.
sentences.n: raddaytu, 'I put back', is a Middle Arabic form of raddadtu: the doubled root is treated like a weak verb. The print is رديت and I vocalise it as it stands. muṣāgh is wrought jewellery, from ṣāgha 'to fashion'.

sentences.t: وَغَسَلْتُ وَلَبِسْتُ ثِيَابًا نَظِيفَةً وَأَخَذْتُ بَقِيَّةَ مَالِي وَخَرَجْتُ مِنَ الْبَيْتِ وَقَفَلْتُهُ
sentences.tr: wa-ghasaltu wa-labistu thiyāban naẓīfatan wa-akhadhtu baqiyyata mālī wa-kharajtu mina al-bayti wa-qafaltuhu
sentences.l: and I washed, and I put-on clean clothes, and I took the remainder of my money, and I went-out from the house and locked it
sentences.i: I washed, put on clean clothes, took what was left of my money, went out of the house, and locked it.

sentences.t: وَجِئْتُ لِصَاحِبِ الْقَاعَةِ وَشَجَّعْتُ نَفْسِي وَدَفَعْتُ لَهُ أُجْرَةَ سَنَةٍ وَقُلْتُ لَهُ أَنَا مُسَافِرٌ إِلَى أَعْمَامِي بِمِصْرَ
sentences.tr: wa-jiʾtu li-ṣāḥibi al-qāʿati wa-shajjaʿtu nafsī wa-dafaʿtu lahu ujrata sanatin wa-qultu lahu anā musāfirun ilā aʿmāmī bi-Miṣra
sentences.l: and I came to the owner of the hall, and I emboldened my self, and I paid to him a year's rent, and I said to him: I a-traveller to my paternal-uncles in Miṣr
sentences.i: I went to the owner of the hall, steeled my courage, paid him a year's rent, and told him, "I am travelling to my uncles in Egypt."
sentences.n: shajjaʿtu nafsī, 'I emboldened myself', means he screwed up his nerve to face the man. Miṣr is Egypt (here the country, with Cairo its centre); aʿmām are paternal uncles.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ سَافَرْتُ إِلَى مِصْرَ وَاجْتَمَعْتُ بِأَعْمَامِي فَفَرِحُوا بِي وَوَجَدْتُهُمْ قَدْ فَرَغُوا مِنْ بَيْعِ مَتْجَرِهِمْ
sentences.tr: thumma sāfartu ilā Miṣra wa-ijtamaʿtu bi-aʿmāmī fa-fariḥū bī wa-wajadtuhum qad faraghū min bayʿi matjarihim
sentences.l: then I travelled to Miṣr and met-with my paternal-uncles, so they rejoiced in me, and I found them having finished from the sale of their merchandise
sentences.i: Then I travelled to Egypt and met my uncles, who were glad of me; I found they had finished selling their merchandise.
sentences.n: ijtamaʿtu bi- is 'I met (joined) with'. matjar is trade, or the goods one trades in.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالُوا لِي مَا سَبَبُ مَجِيئِكَ فَقُلْتُ لَهُمْ اشْتَقْتُ لَكُمْ وَلَمْ أُعْلِمْهُمْ أَنَّ مَعِي شَيْئًا مِنْ مَالِي
sentences.tr: thumma qālū lī mā sababu majīʾika fa-qultu lahum ishtaqtu lakum wa-lam uʿlimhum anna maʿī shayʾan min mālī
sentences.l: then they said to me: what the cause of your coming? So I said to them: I-longed for you; and I did not inform-them that with me was something of my money
sentences.i: Then they asked me, "What brings you here?" I said, "I longed to see you," and I did not let them know that I had any of my money with me.

sentences.t: فَأَقَمْتُ عِنْدَهُمْ سَنَةً وَأَنَا أَتَفَرَّجُ عَلَي مِصْرَ وَنِيلِهَا وَحَطَّيْتُ يَدِي فِي بَقِيَّةِ مَالِي وَصِرْتُ أَصْرِفُ مِنْهُ وَآكُلُ وَأَشْرَبُ
sentences.tr: fa-aqamtu ʿindahum sanatan wa-anā atafarraju ʿalā Miṣra wa-nīlihā wa-ḥaṭṭaytu yadī fī baqiyyati mālī wa-ṣirtu aṣrifu minhu wa-ākulu wa-ashrabu
sentences.l: so I stayed with them a year, and I sight-seeing upon Miṣr and its Nile; and I put my hand into the remainder of my money, and became spending from it and eating and drinking
sentences.i: I stayed with them a year, seeing the sights of Egypt and its Nile, and I dipped into what remained of my money and spent from it, eating and drinking.
sentences.n: ʿalā is printed علي, with the dotted ya; read it as the preposition 'on', not ʿalayya 'upon me'. atafarraju ʿalā, 'I sightsee', is a colloquial turn. ṣirtu aṣrifu, 'I became spending', is the usual Middle Arabic way of saying 'I took to spending'.

sentences.t: حَتَّى قَرُبَ سَفَرُ أَعْمَامِي فَهَرَبْتُ وَاخْتَفَيْتُ مِنْهُمْ
sentences.tr: ḥattā qaruba safaru aʿmāmī fa-harabtu wa-ikhtafaytu minhum
sentences.l: until the journey of my paternal-uncles drew-near, so I fled and hid from them
sentences.i: When my uncles' time of departure drew near, I ran away and hid from them.

sentences.t: فَفَتَّشُوا عَلَيَّ فَلَمْ يَسْمَعُولِي خَبَرًا فَقَالُوا يَكُونُ رَجَعَ إِلَى دِمَشْقَ فَسَافَرُوا
sentences.tr: fa-fattashū ʿalayya fa-lam yasmaʿūlī khabaran fa-qālū yakūnu rajaʿa ilā Dimashqa fa-sāfarū
sentences.l: so they searched upon me, and did not hear-for-me any news; so they said: he-is (perhaps) returned to Damascus; and they travelled
sentences.i: They searched for me and could hear no news of me, so they said, "He must have gone back to Damascus," and they set out.
sentences.n: yasmaʿūlī is printed as one word, yasmaʿū + lī, 'they heard of me' (lit. 'heard for me'); the verb has lost its final alif of the plural, as often in print. yakūnu rajaʿa, 'he is probably returned', is the Middle Arabic way to say 'he has most likely gone back'.

sentences.t: وَخَرَجْتُ أَنَا فَأَقَمْتُ بِمِصْرَ ثَلَٰثَ سِنِينَ حَتَّى لَمْ يَبْقَ مَعِي مِنَ الْمَالِ شَيْءٌ
sentences.tr: wa-kharajtu anā fa-aqamtu bi-Miṣra thalātha sinīna ḥattā lam yabqa maʿī mina al-māli shayʾun
sentences.l: and I came-out, I, and stayed in Miṣr three years until there did not remain with me of the money a thing
sentences.i: Then I came out of hiding and stayed in Egypt three years, until not a thing was left to me of the money.
sentences.n: ثلث is printed without its alif for thalāth, 'three'; the dagger alif supplies it.

sentences.t: وَأَنَا فِي كُلِّ سَنَةٍ أُرْسِلُ لِصَاحِبِ الْقَاعَةِ إِلَى دِمَشْقَ أُجْرَتَهَا وَبَعْدَ الثَّلَٰثِ سِنِينَ ضَاقَ صَدْرِي وَلَمْ يَبْقَ مَعِي إِلَّا أُجْرَةُ السَّنَةِ فَقَطْ
sentences.tr: wa-anā fī kulli sanatin ursilu li-ṣāḥibi al-qāʿati ilā Dimashqa ujratahā wa-baʿda al-thalāthi sinīna ḍāqa ṣadrī wa-lam yabqa maʿī illā ujratu al-sanati faqaṭ
sentences.l: and I, in every year, was-sending to the owner of the hall, to Damascus, its rent; and after the three years my chest grew-narrow, and there did not remain with me save the rent of the year, only
sentences.i: Every year I had been sending the hall's rent to its owner in Damascus. After the three years I grew heavy of heart, with nothing left to me but one year's rent.
sentences.n: baʿda al-thalāth sinīn puts the article on the number, 'after the three years', where Classical would say baʿda thalāthi sinīna; it is a Middle Arabic feature. ḍāqa ṣadrī, 'my chest narrowed', means to be distressed. faqaṭ, 'only', is a late usage.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ سَافَرْتُ إِلَى أَنْ وَصَلْتُ إِلَى دِمَشْقَ وَنَزَلْتُ الْقَاعَةَ فَفَرِحَ بِي صَاحِبُهَا وَوَجَدْتُ الْمَخَازِنَ مُقَفَّلَةً كَمَا كَانَتْ فَفَتَحْتُهَا وَأَخْرَجْتُ الْحَوَائِجَ الَّتِي فِيهَا
sentences.tr: thumma sāfartu ilā an waṣaltu ilā Dimashqa wa-nazaltu al-qāʿata fa-fariḥa bī ṣāḥibuhā wa-wajadtu al-makhāzina muqaffalatan kamā kānat fa-fataḥtuhā wa-akhrajtu al-ḥawāʾija allatī fīhā
sentences.l: then I travelled until I arrived at Damascus, and alighted at the hall, and its owner rejoiced in me; and I found the storerooms locked as they were, so I opened them and brought-out the needs that were in them
sentences.i: Then I travelled until I reached Damascus and took up my lodging in the hall, where its owner welcomed me gladly. I found the storerooms locked just as they had been; I opened them and took out the goods that were inside.
sentences.n: ilā an waṣaltu, 'until I arrived', literally 'to that I arrived'. al-ḥawāʾij, 'needs', is the Middle Arabic word for belongings or goods.

sentences.t: فَوَجَدْتُ تَحْتَ الْفِرَاشِ الَّذِي كُنْتُ نَائِمًا عَلَيْهِ تِلْكَ اللَّيْلَةَ مَعَ الصَّبِيَّةِ الَّتِي ذُبِحَتْ طَوْقَ ذَهَبٍ مُرَصَّعًا بِجَوَاهِرَ
sentences.tr: fa-wajadtu taḥta al-firāshi alladhī kuntu nāʾiman ʿalayhi tilka al-laylata maʿa al-ṣabiyyati allatī dhubiḥat ṭawqa dhahabin muraṣṣaʿan bi-jawāhira
sentences.l: then I found beneath the mattress which I was sleeping upon, that night, with the girl who was-slaughtered, a collar of gold set with jewels
sentences.i: Beneath the mattress on which I had lain that night with the girl who was killed, I found a collar of gold set with jewels.
sentences.n: The object (ṭawqa dhahabin, 'a golden collar') is held to the end of the sentence, after the long relative clause. bi-jawāhira after muraṣṣaʿ marks what the collar is studded with.

sentences.t: فَأَخَذْتُهُ وَمَسَحْتُهُ مِنْ دَمِ الصَّبِيَّةِ الْمَذْبُوحَةِ وَتَأَمَّلْتُهُ وَبَكَيْتُ سَاعَةً ثُمَّ أَقَمْتُ يَوْمَيْنِ وَفِى الْيَوْمِ الثَّالِثِ دَخَلْتُ الْحَمَّامَ وَغَيَّرْتُ أَثْوَابِي
sentences.tr: fa-akhadhtuhu wa-masaḥtuhu min dami al-ṣabiyyati al-madhbūḥati wa-taʾammaltuhu wa-bakaytu sāʿatan thumma aqamtu yawmayni wa-fī al-yawmi al-thālithi dakhaltu al-ḥammāma wa-ghayyartu athwābī
sentences.l: so I took it, and wiped it from the blood of the girl the slaughtered, and gazed-at it, and wept an hour; then I stayed two days, and on the third day I entered the bath and changed my clothes
sentences.i: I took it, wiped the blood of the murdered girl from it, looked at it and wept for an hour. Then I stayed two days, and on the third day I went to the bath and changed my clothes.
sentences.n: masaḥtuhu min dami, 'I wiped it from the blood', means wiped the blood off it.

sentences.t: وَأَنَا مَا مَعِي مِنَ الدَّرَاهِمِ شَيْ فَجِيتُ يَوْمًا إِلَى السُّوقِ
sentences.tr: wa-anā mā maʿī mina al-darāhimi shay fa-jītu yawman ilā al-sūqi
sentences.l: and I, nothing was with me of the dirhams, so I came one day to the market
sentences.i: I had not a dirham to my name, so one day I came to the market.
sentences.n: ما معي من الدراهم شي is a nominal clause with no verb, 'with me, of dirhams, a thing' (a colloquial negation). shay is the shortened spelling of shayʾ. fajītu is the colloquial jītu for jiʾtu, 'I came'.

sentences.t: فَوَسْوَسَ لِى الشَّيْطَانُ لِأَجْلِ إِنْفَاذِ الْقَدَرِ فَأَخَذْتُ عِقْدَ الْجَوْهَرِ وَتَوَجَّهْتُ بِهِ إِلَى السُّوقِ وَنَاوَلْتُهُ لِلدَّلَّالِ فَقَامَ وَأَجْلَسَنِي بِجَانِبِ صَاحِبِ الدَّارِ
sentences.tr: fa-waswasa lī al-shayṭānu li-ajli infādhi al-qadari fa-akhadhtu ʿiqda al-jawhari wa-tawajjahtu bihi ilā al-sūqi wa-nāwaltuhu li-al-dallāli fa-qāma wa-ajlasanī bi-jānibi ṣāḥibi al-dāri
sentences.l: so whispered to me the devil for the sake of the carrying-out of the decree; so I took the necklace of jewels, and set-out with it to the market, and handed it to the broker; so he rose and seated me beside the owner of the house
sentences.i: Then Satan whispered to me, that the decree of fate might be carried out. I took the jewelled necklace, set out with it for the market, and handed it to the broker, who rose and seated me beside the owner of the house.
sentences.n: li-ajli infādhi al-qadar, 'to carry out the decree', is the narrator's way of saying that what followed was fated. ṣāḥib al-dār, 'the owner of the house', is the proprietor of the place where the sale was held.

sentences.t: وَصَبَرَ حَتَّى عَمَرَ السُّوقُ وَأَخَذَهُ الدَّلَّالُ وَنَادَى عَلَيْهِ خُفْيَةً وَأَنَا لَا أَعْلَمُ وَإِذَا الْعِقْدُ مُثَمَّنٌ جَابَ أَلْفَيْنِ دِينَارًا فَجَاءَنِي الدَّلَّالُ
sentences.tr: wa-ṣabara ḥattā ʿamara al-sūqu wa-akhadhahu al-dallālu wa-nādā ʿalayhi khufyatan wa-anā lā aʿlamu wa-idhā al-ʿiqdu muthammanun jāba alfayni dīnāran fa-jāʾanī al-dallālu
sentences.l: and he waited until the market filled, and the broker took it and called upon it secretly, and I not knowing; and behold, the necklace was valued, it brought two-thousand dinars; and the broker came to me
sentences.i: He waited until the market was full; then the broker took it and cried it for sale in secret, without my knowing. And behold, the necklace was appraised and fetched two thousand dinars, and the broker came to me
sentences.n: nādā ʿalayhi, 'he called upon it', is auction language, to cry an item for bids. jāba is the colloquial 'brought' (for jāʾa bi-), here 'fetched'. I read muthamman as 'appraised, priced' (passive of thammana), a guess since the print is unpointed.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ هَذَا الْعِقْدُ عِقْدُ نُحَاسٍ مَصْنُوعٌ صَنْعَةَ الْإِ فْرَنْجِ وَقَدْ وَصَلَ ثَمَنُهُ أَلْفَ دِرْهَمٍ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla hādhā al-ʿiqdu ʿiqdu nuḥāsin maṣnūʿun ṣanʿata al-i franji wa-qad waṣala thamanuhu alfa dirhamin
sentences.l: and said: this necklace is a necklace of copper, made in-the-make of the Franks, and its price has reached a thousand dirhams
sentences.i: and said, "This necklace is a necklace of copper, made in the Frankish manner, and its price has reached a thousand dirhams."
sentences.n: The print splits al-Ifranj ('the Franks', Europeans) into two words, الا فرنج; I keep the break and read them together. The broker's low figure is a trick, and so is the narrator's reply.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهُ نَعَمْ هَذَا كُنَّا صُغْنَاهُ لِوَاحِدَةٍ نَضْحَكُ عَلَيْهَا بِهِ وَوَرِثَتْهُ زَوْجَتِي فَأَرَدْنَا بَيْعَهُ فَرُحْ أَقْبِضُ الْأَلْفَ دِرْهَمٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahu naʿam hādhā kunnā ṣughnāhu li-wāḥidatin naḍḥaku ʿalayhā bihi wa-warithathu zawjatī fa-aradnā bayʿahu fa-ruḥ aqbiḍu al-alfa dirhamin
sentences.l: so I said to him: yes, this, we had fashioned it for a woman we would laugh upon with it; and my wife inherited it, and we wished its sale; so go, I-receive the thousand dirhams
sentences.i: I said to him, "Yes. We had this made for a woman we meant to make fools of with it; my wife inherited it, and we wanted to sell it. Go, then, and I will take the thousand dirhams."
sentences.n: naḍḥaku ʿalayhā, 'we laugh upon her', means to make fun of, or cheat, someone. The last clause is obscure in the print: I read فرح as the imperative fa-ruḥ ('go') followed by aqbiḍu ('I will take'); fa-raḥ is a possible alternative, but it would make no clear sense. The narrator accepts the false price to keep the sale quiet. I give my best reading, not a certain one.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَ زَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka Shahra Zāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: and the morning overtook Shahr Zād, so she fell-silent from the permitted speech
sentences.i: And morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted speech.
sentences.n: The closing formula. 'The permitted speech' (al-kalām al-mubāḥ) is the stock phrase for storytelling that a wise woman may lawfully stop; it also rhymes with al-ṣabāḥ. The print divides Shahrazād into two words.
